en.p: As shown in the figure, in triangle $\mathrm{ABC}$, take point $\mathrm{D}$ on segment $\mathrm{AB}$ with $\overline{\mathrm{AD}}:\overline{\mathrm{DB}}=3:2$, let $O$ be the circle centered at $\mathrm{A}$ passing through $\mathrm{D}$, and let $\mathrm{E}$ be the point where circle $O$ meets segment $\mathrm{AC}$.

We have $\sin A:\sin C=8:5$, and the ratio of the areas of triangle $\mathrm{ADE}$ and triangle $\mathrm{ABC}$ is $9:35$. When the radius of the circumcircle of triangle $\mathrm{ABC}$ is $7$, what is the maximum area of triangle $\mathrm{PBC}$ for a point $\mathrm{P}$ on circle $O$? (Given that $\overline{\mathrm{AB}}<\overline{\mathrm{AC}}$.) [4 points]
